conventions: p is prime. K is complete discretely valued of characteristic zero, with perfect countable residue field k of characteristic p; F=W(k)[1/p], Fⁿʳ is its maximal unramified extension inside K̄, and C is the completion of K̄. All analytic spaces are separated, taut and countable at infinity, as in §1.3.3, pp.7–8. A completed unramified coefficient field is used only where explicitly stated, never silently substituted for Fⁿʳ.

Nφ=pφN. Period tensors use diagonal operators; the imported B_st coordinate has N=−d/du. Every monodromy-untwisting formula must be adjusted to that sign. t has φ(t)=pt, and {−r} on HK multiplies φ by p⁻ʳ. Derived joint invariants, derived completed tensors, and natural locally convex Q_p topologies are part of the analytic input.

LH(C_Q_p) is the abelian left heart of the strict derived category of locally convex Q_p spaces. Tildes refer to left-heart cohomology; untilded groups are its classical part. VS is the source’s Vector Space functor category, TVS is the functor category of Definition 4.1: functors from sympathetic algebras into LH(C_Q_p), with uniform boundedness for algebra maps. Its morphisms are natural transformations. Evaluation at C is an ordinary locally convex space only for classical objects, and arbitrary continuous maps on C-points are not TVS morphisms. The change from VS to TVS needs its precise comparison theorem.

FilʳHⁱ means the image of Hⁱ(FʳRΓ) in Hⁱ(RΓ); Fʳⁱ denotes the former group itself. The kernel Aʳⁱ is often large and torsion. The square has u=(a,b) and v=(c,−d). Finite BC height is signed, qBC height extends it, and ht(Q_p)=1 while a reasonable torsion B_dR⁺-Pair has height zero.

For small X the induced F⁰ lattice in Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR) defines the filtered HK bundle. Smallness requires finite free B_dR⁺ cohomology in every degree. General Conjectures 6.21 and 9.1 are not promoted to unconditional theorem targets.

nodes.title: Filtered modules with a de Rham lattice
nodes.statement: A filtered (φ,N)-module over C is a pair (M,L): M is finite dimensional over Fⁿʳ, φ is a bijective σ-semilinear map, N is Fⁿʳ-linear with Nφ=pφN, and L is a finite free B_dR⁺-submodule of M⊗B_dR spanning that module after inverting t. Morphisms are φ,N-equivariant maps carrying L into L′. The topology and period embeddings are the imported ones; C is not embedded canonically in B_dR⁺.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use the existing finite Frobenius–monodromy coefficients over Fⁿʳ; add only the lattice datum.
Use localization to express spanning and the induced period-linear morphism.
acceptance: Identity and composition preserve the lattice.
No Galois action is required over C.

nodes.title: Cohomological criteria for acyclicity
nodes.statement: For a pair (M,L), acyclicity is equivalent to H¹(E(M,L))=0, to surjectivity of (M⊗B_st)^{N=0,φ=1}→(M⊗B_dR)/L, and to the existence of a sublattice L′⊆L for which (M,L′) is weakly admissible. Weak admissibility is equivalent to E≅O^rank(M), and also to finite Q_p-dimension of V_st together with exactness of its fundamental sequence. In that case V_st⊗B_st≅M⊗B_st and V_st⊗B_dR⁺≅L.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Apply classification and H⁰/H¹ of slope bundles.
Compute H¹ as the cokernel of the period-to-lattice-quotient map using the two-chart complex.
Shrink a lattice to a slope-zero modification using the argument of Lemma 5.3; classification identifies its sections and period evaluations.

sources.match: Identifies slope, cohomology, period-surjectivity and smaller-lattice criteria.

nodes.title: Bounded eigenspaces and period kernels
nodes.statement: For r∈N, M with φ-slopes in [0,r], and a lattice L satisfying M⊗tʳB_dR⁺⊆tʳL⊆M⊗B_dR⁺, define the VS-valued X_stʳ(M)=(M⊗B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=pʳ} and V_stʳ(M,L)=ker(X_stʳ(M)→(M⊗B_dR⁺)/tʳL). The bounded positive ring is essential: the displayed quotient map is not defined on the unrestricted B_st eigenspace. In the acyclic case this is a short exact sequence and V_stʳ=tʳV_st inside M⊗B_dR. More generally for k≥0 the t⁻ᵏB_st⁺-version maps onto (M⊗t⁻ᵏB_dR⁺)/tʳL iff the pair is acyclic, with the same kernel. For any such M, X_stʳ(M) is a finite BC object of curvature ≤0 and height dim M: it is H⁰ of the nonnegative-slope bundle attached to M{−r} with lattice M⊗B_dR⁺.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Form invariant subobjects of the imported period Vector Spaces and the indicated kernel.

Use the VB1 gluing comparison to identify X_stʳ(M) with H⁰(E(M{−r},M⊗B_dR⁺)); its slopes are r minus the Newton slopes of M. Standard-bundle cohomology, the Le Bras equivalence and Euler height give finite BC, curvature ≤0 and height dim M.
Use Remark 5.16 and the graded comparison of successive t-denominator levels to prove the criterion.
acceptance: All maps are natural Vector Space maps and agree on C-points.

Choose an admissible lattice and use its finite-dimensional period realization to force B_st-valued functionals to have B_st coefficients.

nodes.title: Period reconstruction modulo a power of t
nodes.statement: Under the same acyclicity and boundedness assumptions, for k≥2r the evaluation map M∨⊗(B_dR⁺/tᵏ)→Hom_VS(V_stʳ(M,L),B_dR⁺/tᵏ) has kernel killed by tʳ and cokernel killed by t²ʳ. In particular both are killed by t²ʳ. No isomorphism for finite k is asserted.

Compare the kernels for L′ and L; their quotient is killed by tʳ.

Fʳⁱ is not identified with Filʳⁱ.

nodes.title: The fundamental diagram
nodes.statement: For every smooth dagger X/C and 0≤i≤r form the natural commutative square with upper row H̃ʳⁱ→X̃ʳⁱ and lower row F̃ʳⁱ→B̃ⁱ, using the syntomic period map and the map of triangles with common term RΓ_dR/Fʳ. The general assertion that this square is bicartesian is Conjecture 6.21, not an unconditional theorem.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Form the syntomic and filtered de Rham triangles and their compatible maps.
Take left-heart cohomology and the truncation isomorphism α_r.
Use the existing BicartesianSq predicate; in the abelian left heart it is equivalent to the sequence 0→H̃→X̃⊕F̃→B̃→0 being exact, with the stated minus sign.
acceptance: Both routes around the square agree; their difference, rather than their sum, kills u.

tests.name: FundamentalDiagram.not_forget_topology
tests.statement: Exactness of a sequence of underlying vector spaces alone does not certify BicartesianSq in LH(C_Q_p); a dense nonclosed inclusion must retain its left-heart cokernel.

uses.how: Identifies both obstructions to bicartesianness.
States the comparison delivered for the proved classes.

nodes.title: Twist invariance and the surjectivity reduction
nodes.statement: For fixed i≥0 the fundamental square is bicartesian for one r≥i iff it is so for every r≥i. Multiplication by t identifies H̃ʳⁱ with H̃ʳ⁺¹ⁱ and F̃ʳ⁺¹ⁱ=tF̃ʳⁱ; the quotient Xʳ⁺¹ⁱ/tXʳⁱ identifies with Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗̂C and the corresponding Bⁱ/tBⁱ with Hⁱ_dR(X), by Hyodo–Kato. For a fixed r, surjectivity of Xʳⁱ⊕Fʳⁱ→Bⁱ in all degrees 0≤i≤r yields the short exact left-heart sequences in that range by induction from degree −1=0.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Apply the exact rows and columns for t multiplication; the bottom comparison is an isomorphism.
Apply the long exact cohomology sequence of the syntomic fiber; preceding-degree surjectivity kills the left kernel.
acceptance: Surjectivity at a single isolated degree is not used to infer injectivity at the same degree.

sources.match: Reduces all twists to a single twist and the full comparison to surjectivity.

nodes.title: Proper analytic comparison over K
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper rigid analytic X_K/K, with X=X_K×C, all cohomology groups below are finite dimensional and there is a natural B_st-linear G_K-equivariant isomorphism Hⁱ_ét(X,Q_p)⊗B_st≅Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗B_st preserving φ and N. It induces the filtered B_dR comparison with Hⁱ_dR(X_K)⊗_K B_dR. No semistable model is assumed. The induced dual Hom descriptions are strict for the natural weak Hom topologies.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Construct the map using α_s for s>i and untwist by tˢ.
Use finite-dimensional étale cohomology and finite BC Dimension to split the syntomic sequence.
Identify the filtered arithmetic module as weakly admissible and apply its period evaluations; verify independence of s and strictness.
acceptance: On a proper semistable model this is the imported CP.4 comparison, with its Nφ=pφN convention.

sources.match: Removes the semistable-model condition in the proper rigid setting.

nodes.title: Proper analytic comparison over C
nodes.statement: For X/C smooth proper rigid analytic and i≥0 there are natural B_st-linear isomorphisms Hⁱ_ét(X,Q_p)⊗B_st≅Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗B_st preserving φ,N and inducing a filtered B_dR isomorphism with Bⁱ⊗_{B_dR⁺}B_dR. The filtration on Bⁱ is im(Hⁱ(FʲRΓ_dR)→Bⁱ). In particular the associated pair (Hⁱ_HK,F⁰(Bⁱ[1/t])) is weakly admissible. This does not identify its lattice with the unfiltered Bⁱ.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use the finite-rank proper cohomology and finite-length graded filtered quotients.
Split the syntomic sequence by the same BC argument as over K.
Show Bⁱ/FilˢBⁱ→Hⁱ(RΓ_dR/Fˢ) is bijective using its injectivity from the image definition and surjectivity from the period sequence.
Apply the weak-admissible lattice criterion.
acceptance: The identification uses F⁰(Bⁱ[1/t]), not Bⁱ in general.

sources.match: Proves the proper C comparison with its actual induced cohomological filtration.

nodes.title: The simplified Stein and affinoid diagram
nodes.statement: For a smooth dagger Stein space or dagger affinoid X/C and r≥0 there is a natural map between strictly exact rows 0→Ωʳ⁻¹(X)/ker d→Hʳ_proét(X,Q_p(r))→Xʳʳ→0 and 0→Ωʳ⁻¹(X)/ker d —d→ Ωʳ(X)^{d=0}→Hʳ_dR(X)→0. The left vertical map is identity, the right is ι_HK⊗θ, and the middle β̃=p⁻ʳβα_r⁻¹. All vertical maps are strict with closed image. Hʳ_proét is Fréchet in the Stein case and LB in the affinoid case; ker β̃≅(Hʳ_HK(X)⊗̂B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=p^{r−1}}. Set Ω⁻¹=0.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Import the syntomic Stein diagram and α_r in degree r.
Normalize the middle map by p⁻ʳ to preserve symbols.
Transport the topology, strictness and kernel assertions through α_r.
acceptance: The top row is pro-étale, and its differential-form kernel on a disc is nonzero.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.14, p. 43; its cited part-I Corollary 6.9 and Proposition 5.13
sources.match: Transfers the simplified syntomic diagram to pro-étale cohomology, including topology.

nodes.title: Bicartesian diagrams for proper, Stein and affinoid spaces
nodes.statement: The fundamental square is bicartesian for smooth proper X/C and for smooth dagger Stein or affinoid X/C, in all 0≤i≤r by twist invariance. At degree i=r the proper horizontal arrows are injective and Fʳʳ→Filʳʳ is an isomorphism. At degree r in the Stein/affinoid case both horizontal arrows are surjective with common kernel Ωʳ⁻¹/ker d. The latter assertion uses pro-étale cohomology, not étale cohomology of a rigid affinoid completion.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: For the proper case use the short exact period sequence and the filtered quotient identification.
For Stein/affinoid spaces compare the two triangles, use Hʲ(RΓ_dR/Fʳ)=0 for j≥r, and identify the two kernels by reduction to C.
Apply twist invariance for other i≤r.
acceptance: A proper point tests horizontal injectivity; a dagger disc in degree one tests the shared nonzero kernel.

sources.match: Establishes the two initial geometric cases and distinguishes their horizontal maps.

nodes.title: Bundle cohomology measuring the diagram
nodes.statement: For small X, i≥0, r≥0 and n=0,1 put hⁿ_i(r)=Hⁿ(X_FF,E(Hⁱ_HK(X){−r},FilʳHⁱ_dR(X/B_dR))), as a finite BC object. Here {−r} multiplies φ by p⁻ʳ and leaves N fixed, and the lattice is the induced Filʳ lattice in Bⁱ[1/t]. Use hⁿ_{−1}(r)=0. In the range i≤r, or for quasi-compact X with r≥dim X, the tʳ-period isomorphism identifies this modified bundle with the untwisted pair (Hⁱ_HK,F⁰Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR)); the simultaneous change of φ and lattice is essential.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Apply the filtered-module bundle construction to the finite cohomology module and its image lattice.
Use the finite BC realization of H⁰ and H¹ of a coherent bundle.
Use t multiplication and the filtration shift in the range i≤r to identify the twisted and untwisted pairs.
acceptance: The lattice uses the image filtration; Aʳⁱ is not part of that lattice.

sources.locator: §7.2.2 and Lemma 7.7, p. 47; proof of Proposition 7.10, p. 48
sources.match: Introduces the finite bundle-cohomology objects controlling both ends of the comparison sequence.

api.name: FailureObjects.h0
api.statement: The zeroth object is H⁰ of the indicated modified bundle.

api.name: FailureObjects.h1
api.statement: The first object is H¹ of that bundle.

api.name: FailureObjects.map
api.statement: Compatible pullbacks on filtered HK modules induce maps of hⁿ, preserving identity and composition.

api.name: FailureObjects.twist
api.statement: Simultaneously twisting φ and the lattice by tʳ identifies the bundle and its cohomology with the untwisted F⁰ pair.

tests.name: FailureObjects.point
tests.statement: For a point at i=r=0 the bundle is O, so h⁰=Q_p and h¹=0.

tests.name: FailureObjects.shifted_point
tests.statement: For a point at i=0,r=1, φ=p⁻¹ and lattice tB_dR⁺ cancel to give O again; twisting only the lattice would give O(−1).

tests.name: FailureObjects.rank_zero
tests.statement: A zero HK group with zero lattice gives h⁰=h¹=0.

uses.how: Identifies the left kernel and right cokernel.
Acyclicity of these bundles is the criterion used in geometric cases.

nodes.title: Kernel and cokernel descriptions
nodes.statement: For small X and i≤r, h⁰_i(r)≅ker(Xʳⁱ⊕Filʳⁱ→Bⁱ)≅ker(Xʳⁱ→Bⁱ/Filʳⁱ), and h¹_i(r) is the corresponding cokernel. Moreover ker(Hʳⁱ→Xʳⁱ⊕Fʳⁱ)≅h¹_{i−1}(r). These identifications lift to the natural TVS objects, with the difference-map convention of CS.1.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: The two-chart cohomology complex gives the first two identities.
Compare the syntomic and filtered de Rham long exact sequences with their common DR term.
Apply the snake lemma; multiplying Fʳⁱ by tʳ kills its torsion and identifies its image in Bⁱ, justifying the reduced bottom row.
acceptance: At i=0 the preceding-degree kernel is zero.

sources.match: Computes the two failure terms by an explicit comparison of exact rows.

nodes.title: The canonical qBC filtration on pro-étale cohomology
nodes.statement: For small X and 0≤i≤r the natural TVS Hʳⁱ is a qBC. Its functorial canonical filtration has successive curvature pieces Hʳⁱ_{>0}≅h¹_{i−1}(r), Hʳⁱ_{=0}≅Aʳⁱ=(Fʳⁱ)_{B_dR⁺-tors}, and Hʳⁱ_{<0}≅h⁰_i(r). The middle piece is a reasonable B_dR⁺-Pair and need not be finite BC. These are associated graded objects, not a canonical direct-sum decomposition. Zero pieces are allowed in every curvature class.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use the diagram of CS.2/failure-kernel-cokernel to filter H by successive kernels.
Identify the middle quotient with ker(F→B).
Apply the imported qBC three-piece recognition and uniqueness theorem; finite bundle H¹ and H⁰ provide the positive and negative curvature pieces.
acceptance: The assertion does not replace an infinite torsion Pair by a finite-length module.

sources.match: Constructs the filtration from the cohomological diagram and identifies all its graded pieces.

api.name: ProetaleQBC.positive
api.statement: The first subobject is h¹_{i−1}(r), with its canonical injection into Hʳⁱ.

api.name: ProetaleQBC.zero_piece
api.statement: The middle graded piece equals Aʳⁱ and its B_dR⁺-torsion description.

api.name: ProetaleQBC.negative
api.statement: The final quotient is h⁰_i(r).

api.name: ProetaleQBC.naturality
api.statement: Dagger pullback preserves the filtration and induces the expected bundle maps on its finite graded pieces.

api.name: ProetaleQBC.finite_agreement
api.statement: When H is already finite BC, its filtration agrees with the existing finite BC curvature filtration; the qBC height restricts to the BC height.

tests.name: ProetaleQBC.proper
tests.statement: For proper X the only nonzero piece is the finite Q_p negative-curvature piece Hʳ_proét; the positive and torsion pieces vanish.

tests.name: ProetaleQBC.disc
tests.statement: For the dagger disc at i=r=1, HK¹=0, so both finite pieces vanish while A¹¹=O(X)/C and H¹_proét≅A¹¹.

tests.name: ProetaleQBC.point
tests.statement: For a point in degree zero the negative piece is Q_p of height one, not curvature zero merely because it has C-dimension zero.

uses.how: Separates finite height errors from the height-zero Pair.
Its torsion Pair has zero maps into period fields.

nodes.title: The exact sequence with two failure terms
nodes.statement: For small X and 0≤i≤r there is a natural exact sequence of TVS objects 0→h¹_{i−1}(r)→Hʳⁱ→Fʳⁱ⊕Xʳⁱ→Bⁱ→h¹_i(r)→0, with the signs transported from CS.1. Consequently the fundamental diagram in degree i is bicartesian exactly when both h¹_{i−1}(r) and h¹_i(r) vanish.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Combine the kernel description with the canonical qBC filtration.
The image of F→B is Fil, so adjoining F does not change the right cokernel.
Compare the classical sequence with the left-heart sequence using the classical X,B corners and the strict analytic comparison.
acceptance: The criterion requires the preceding-degree failure term as well as the degree-i term.

sources.match: Displays both obstructions; killing only the right one is insufficient.

nodes.title: The height formula and its sign
nodes.statement: For small X and r≥0, ht(Hʳʳ)=dim_Fⁿʳ Hʳ_HK(X)+ht(h¹_{r−1}(r))+ht(h¹_r(r)). Each h¹ term has height ≤0, and height zero occurs only if that term is zero, because it is H¹ of a vector bundle. Therefore ht(Hʳʳ)≤dim_C Hʳ_dR(X), with equality exactly when both failure terms vanish. This strictness is not asserted for every positive-curvature BC: torsion away from ∞ is a counterexample to that broader assertion.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: The Pair piece has height zero and qBC height is additive.
Apply the imported Euler-height identity ht(H⁰E)−ht(H¹E)=rk E.
Decompose the bundle into slope blocks; each nonzero H¹ block has strictly negative height.
Use the Hyodo–Kato rank comparison.
acceptance: Height is a signed BC/qBC invariant, not the ordinary dimension of an infinite Q_p-vector space.

sources.locator: Proposition 7.10 proof, p. 48; Equation (3.10) and Remark 3.11, p.15; Remark 3.13(iv), p.16
sources.match: Computes the two numerical defects and uses the stronger sign for H¹ of bundles.

nodes.title: The degreewise equivalence of comparison criteria
nodes.statement: For a small smooth dagger X/C and r≥0 the following are equivalent: the fundamental square at degree i=r is bicartesian; h¹_{r−1}(r)=h¹_r(r)=0; the two pairs (Hʲ_HK(X),F⁰Hʲ_dR(X/B_dR)) for j=r−1,r are acyclic; the TVS Hʳʳ and H_syn^{r+1}(X,r) both have curvature ≤0; ht(Hʳʳ)=dim_C Hʳ_dR(X). The degree r+1 term here is syntomic, not H^{r+1}_proét(X,Q_p(r)); it lies outside the comparison range. Negative-degree pairs vanish.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use the failure exact sequence and acyclicity criteria.
Twist the bundle pairs to remove r.
Apply the positive-piece description also to the adjacent syntomic term in the source diagram; do not extend α_r past degree r.
Use the height defect formula and the strict negativity of nonzero bundle H¹.
acceptance: The single-degree curvature condition is not substituted for the pair of degree-r and degree-(r+1) conditions.

sources.match: Equates five conditions, retaining the adjacent syntomic group in the curvature condition.

nodes.title: The four conjectural properties for a small variety
nodes.statement: For a small smooth dagger X/C the following families of statements are equivalent: the fundamental squares are bicartesian for all 0≤i≤r; all pairs (Hⁱ_HK,F⁰Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR)) are acyclic; every Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p) has curvature ≤0; ht(Hⁱ_proét(X,Q_p))=dim_C Hⁱ_dR(X) for every i. This is an equivalence of properties, not a proof that they hold for every small X.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Vary r in the degreewise equivalence and use twist invariance.

For the adjacent positive-curvature piece use the bundle-cohomology twist identification h¹_i(r)≅h¹_i(r+1) from the failure objects. At r+1 the comparison range includes degree r+1; this identifies the finite positive piece needed for the induction. No comparison of the full syntomic group in degree r+1 at twist r is asserted.
acceptance: All degrees are quantified; a height identity in one degree is not used to prove acyclicity in every degree.

sources.locator: Corollary 7.11 and Remark 7.12, p. 48; Conjectures 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4, p. 46
sources.match: Extends the quasi-compact equivalence to the actual finite-free smallness condition.

nodes.title: Splitting the crystalline eigenspace complex
nodes.statement: For a smooth quasi-compact dagger X/C, r≥dim X, and the functorial log-crystalline complex of the analytic package, Hⁱ([RΓ_cris(X)]^{φ=pʳ})≅(Hⁱ_HK(X)⊗B_st⁺)^{N=0,φ=pʳ} as BC objects. The eigenspace complex is quasi-isomorphic to the direct sum of these groups placed in degree i. The splitting depends on cocycle lifts; it is neither canonical nor claimed Galois equivariant. The proof uses the completed unramified coefficient version of HK, with its comparison to the Fⁿʳ version.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use the non-equivariant crystalline–HK comparison.
Decompose each finite HK group into Dieudonné–Manin blocks and choose cocycle lifts of its basis.
Construct maps into the mapping fiber of 1−φ/pʳ by correcting each lifted block with a primitive of its Frobenius discrepancy.
Use the slope bound ≤min(i,dim X) and r≥dim X to identify the eigenspaces and cohomology.
acceptance: Changing cocycle lifts may change the splitting; no naturality assertion is added.

sources.match: Constructs a noncanonical splitting in the dimension-bounded range.

nodes.title: A noncanonical decomposition of syntomic cohomology
nodes.statement: For smooth quasi-compact dagger X/C and r≥dim X, every natural syntomic TVS H_synⁱ(X,r) is isomorphic, noncanonically, to h¹_{i−1}(r)⊕h⁰_i(r)⊕P_i, where P_i is a reasonable B_dR⁺-Pair representing the curvature-zero piece. For i≤r this decomposes pro-étale cohomology through α_r. It does not prove that the canonical qBC filtration splits canonically or that every qBC splits.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Replace the crystalline eigenspace complex by its split cohomology complex.
Represent the syntomic fiber by the explicit three-term total complex and remove an acyclic differential-image complex.
Use finite free de Rham cohomology, compact-type reflexivity, extension of continuous forms and the open mapping theorem to choose period-linear complements.
The remaining kernel and cokernel are h⁰_i and h¹_{i−1}; reduce the middle Pair modulo tʳ.
acceptance: The theorem is independent of the proofs of the final comparison cases: do not make Theorem 8.1 depend on it.

sources.match: Splits the canonical filtration after choices in the stated range.

nodes.title: Varieties with nonnegative de Rham slopes
nodes.statement: A smooth dagger X/C has de Rham slopes ≥0 if X is small and, for every i≥0, the filtered module (Hⁱ_HK(X),F⁰Hⁱ_dR(X/B_dR)) is acyclic. The term refers to slopes of its modified bundle, not to φ-slopes alone and not to nonnegative Hodge–Tate weights.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use smallness to obtain finite filtered modules in every degree.
Apply the acyclic predicate to their induced F⁰ lattices.
acceptance: The smallness condition is included, even when acyclicity is used as shorthand.

sources.match: Defines the hypothesis under which the small-variety comparison is proved.

api.name: DeRhamNonnegative.small
api.statement: The predicate implies smallness.

api.name: DeRhamNonnegative.acyclic
api.statement: For each i the indicated filtered HK module is acyclic.

api.name: DeRhamNonnegative.iso
api.statement: The predicate is preserved by compatible isomorphisms of the full cohomology package.

api.name: DeRhamNonnegative.bicartesian
api.statement: For small X it is equivalent to all fundamental squares being bicartesian, by CS.2/global-equivalence.

api.name: DeRhamNonnegative.height
api.statement: It implies ht(Hⁱ_proét)=dim_C Hⁱ_dR in every degree.

tests.name: DeRhamNonnegative.point
tests.statement: A point has the predicate: its only nonzero bundle is O.

tests.name: DeRhamNonnegative.affinoid
tests.statement: A smooth dagger affinoid has the predicate by the elementary diagram, smallness and CS.2/global-equivalence; in particular the dagger disc does.

tests.name: DeRhamNonnegative.infinite_points
tests.statement: The countable disjoint union of points does not have the predicate, because it is not small even though its components have it.

uses.how: Formulates the three geometric stability results.
Is the common hypothesis of both reconstruction theorems.

nodes.title: Nonnegative de Rham slopes for products
nodes.statement: If smooth dagger X,Y/C have de Rham slopes ≥0, their product has de Rham slopes ≥0. In degree n the cup product gives an injective bundle map ⊕_{i+j=n}E_i(X)⊗E_j(Y)→E_n(X×Y) whose cokernel is coherent and supported at ∞. Equality of the two filtration lattices is not required or asserted.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Apply HK and de Rham Künneth and their compatibility with cup products to establish smallness and identify the punctured bundles.
The filtered cup product gives lattice containment, hence the injection with torsion cokernel at ∞.
Tensor acyclicity annihilates H¹ of the source and torsion sheaves have H¹=0; the long exact sequence annihilates H¹ of the target.
acceptance: The claim is about de Rham/HK Künneth, not a general algebraic tensor-product formula for pro-étale cohomology.

sources.match: Proves product closure using a torsion modification rather than equality of filtrations.

nodes.title: Algebraic analytifications have nonnegative slopes
nodes.statement: For a smooth finite-type algebraic variety V/C, its dagger analytification Vᵃⁿ has de Rham slopes ≥0. For each i, the algebraic admissible filtered module maps to its analytic counterpart, isomorphically on HK; the resulting bundle injection has coherent cokernel supported at ∞. The analytic lattice may be larger than the algebraic one.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use the algebraic period comparison to obtain an admissible algebraic pair.
Apply HK GAGA and analytic de Rham finiteness to obtain smallness and the lattice comparison.
Enlarging the lattice gives a torsion modification; the H¹ sequence transfers acyclicity.
acceptance: The result includes nonproper V; it does not replace analytic pro-étale cohomology by algebraic étale cohomology.

sources.match: Uses algebraic admissibility and Hyodo–Kato GAGA to prove analytic acyclicity.

nodes.title: Almost proper varieties have nonnegative slopes
nodes.statement: Let X/C be smooth proper rigid analytic and Z⊆X any closed analytic subvariety. The smooth dagger complement U=X∖Z has de Rham slopes ≥0. No smoothness or normal crossings assumption on Z is imposed in the conclusion. A proper modification reducing the boundary to a simple normal crossings divisor is a proof input.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Resolve the pair in characteristic zero, without changing U, obtaining a smooth proper X′ with normal crossings boundary D.
Use the logarithmic period exact sequence for the proper pair (X′,D).
Identify ordinary HK and unfiltered de Rham cohomology of U with the log pair and compare logarithmic and naive filtrations.
Surjectivity in the top logarithmic sequence implies it for the fundamental difference map for U in every degree. Apply induction and CS.2/global-equivalence; retain finiteness proving smallness.
acceptance: The boundary may be singular; the resolution input must cover proper rigid pairs, not just affinoid dagger pairs.

sources.match: Proves the complement case by resolving the boundary and comparing with logarithmic cohomology.

nodes.title: The logarithmic and naive filtration discrepancy
nodes.statement: With U=X′∖D a resolved almost proper pair and i≤r, the two-term complexes [Hⁱ_ét(U,Q_p(r))→H̃ⁱ_proét(U,Q_p(r))] and [Hⁱ(FʳRΓ_dR(X′ with log D/B_dR⁺))→H̃ⁱ(FʳRΓ_dR(U/B_dR⁺))] are naturally isomorphic in the derived/left-heart realization. These are complexes with maps; no equality of ordinary quotient vector spaces without strictness is inferred.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Compare the logarithmic period and analytic syntomic triangles.
Their HK and unfiltered de Rham terms are isomorphic.
Cancel those terms in the associated mapping cones.
acceptance: For a proper pair with empty boundary both discrepancy complexes are zero.

sources.match: Identifies the cohomological difference with the difference between the two filtrations.

nodes.title: Comparison for semistable tube complements
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛/O_K be weak formal with local étale charts Spf(O_K{T₁,…,T_n}/(T₁⋯T_s−π)), 1≤s≤m≤n. Let 𝔝 be locally either ⋂_{j=s+1}^mV(T_j) or ⋃_{j=s+1}^mV(T_j), with the stated compatible charts, and assume 𝔛_K smooth proper. For U=]𝔛_k∖𝔝_k[_𝔛, the base change U_C has de Rham slopes ≥0 and hence bicartesian fundamental diagrams. The restriction RΓ_dR(𝔛_K∖𝔝_K)→RΓ_dR(U) is an unfiltered quasi-isomorphism, compatible with the natural filtration map; no filtered-complex quasi-isomorphism is claimed. The compatible HK comparison identifies the underlying coefficients, and naturality gives inclusion of the induced full B_dR⁺ lattices. That inclusion, rather than equality of the filtrations, suffices for acyclicity.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use Grosse-Klönne Corollary 3.8(a),(c) for the unfiltered tube-complement comparison in the stated charts. Proposition 8.3 of CN25 overstates this as a filtered quasi-isomorphism; E16 records the correction.
Apply the almost proper theorem to V=(𝔛_K∖𝔝_K)_C, and use the compatible HK comparison to identify its punctured bundle with that of U_C.

Quasi-compactness of U_C gives smallness. The natural filtration map sends L_V into L_U inside the common localized period module. These are full lattices, so E_i(V)→E_i(U_C) is injective with finite-length cokernel at ∞. Torsion sheaves have H¹=0; the cohomology sequence therefore transfers H¹=0 from E_i(V) to E_i(U_C).
acceptance: Both intersection and union versions require the stated coordinate description; an arbitrary closed formal subscheme is not covered.

For the weak formal projective line and the infinity section, restriction from the affine line to the dagger closed unit disc is not a quasi-isomorphism on gr⁰ of the naive Hodge filtration: (1−πT)⁻¹ is overconvergent on the disc but has a pole on the affine line. This rules out the stronger filtered-complex claim without affecting unfiltered de Rham invariance or the lattice-inclusion argument.

sources.locator: Proposition 8.3 and the following example, pp.51–52, with E16 filtration correction
sources.match: The chart hypotheses and slope application are retained; lattice containment replaces the unjustified filtered-complex equivalence.

sources.locator: Corollary 3.8(a),(c), p.16; Proposition 3.7, pp.14–16, in arXiv v1 pagination
sources.match: Proves the underlying de Rham comparison for both the intersection and union charts; it does not assert an equivalence on the associated graded Hodge complexes.

nodes.title: Small tubular neighbourhoods in projective space
nodes.statement: Let X=Pⁿ_K and let Z=Z₁×_X⋯×_XZ_c be a smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection of c hypersurfaces in the codimension-c setting of Proposition 8.4. There is ε₀∈|K×| such that for positive ε∈|K×| with ε<ε₀, removing the specified tubular neighbourhood Z(ε) instead of Z induces compatible quasi-isomorphisms in de Rham and HK cohomology. The same comparison holds for the union of the Z_j by analytic Čech descent under the source’s complete-intersection hypotheses. The resulting dagger complement over C has de Rham slopes ≥0. The chosen tube definition and its radius inequalities must be part of the geometric supplier. The restriction preserves the induced filtration, but equality of filtration lattices or a filtered-complex quasi-isomorphism is not required: lattice containment transfers acyclicity through a torsion quotient at ∞.
hypotheses: The common conventions and the hypotheses in the statement apply.
proofSteps: Use the local normal-coordinate description along the smooth complete intersection and the unfiltered tube invariance of de Rham cohomology in Grosse-Klönne Proposition 3.7.
Transfer to HK through its comparison and naturality; check analytic Čech descent for all strata used in the union statement. The precise radius and descent compatibility remain part of G-GEOMETRIC.

nodes.title: Cohomology along a countable exhaustion

The global versions are cohomology of the respective derived inverse-limit complexes, not definitions as ordinary limits of groups. In this setting X^{r,i}≅lim X_n^{r,i}, B^i≅lim B_n^i, and R¹lim X_n^{r,i}=R¹lim F̄_n^{r,i}=0.

nodes.title: Étale Künneth with a proper factor
nodes.statement: For smooth rigid analytic Y,T/C with Y proper, cup product gives ⊕_{j≥0}Hʲ_ét(Y,Q_p)⊗_{Q_p}H^{i−j}_ét(T,Q_p)≅Hⁱ_ét(Y×T,Q_p) for every i≥0. The sum is finite in each degree. nodes.title: R¹lim vanishing for proper times Stein

nodes.title: Geometric pro-étale-to-period-module recovery
